stock.title: Garmin stock forecast: where shares could go
stock.meta_description: Garmin stock forecast: weighted value is $277.87 in October 2029, with bear and bull cases of $155.03 and $413.77.
stock.opening: Garmin's weighted forecast is $277.87 in October 2029. It hinges on Fitness carrying growth while Thailand and Mercedes-Benz convert investment into durable profit.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers questions about Garmin's business, rivals, management, and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Garmin's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: Weighted value is $268.75 in October 2027, a −4% return including dividends. It is $277.87 in October 2029, a +3% return. The bear case has a 27% probability, the base case 56%, and the bull case 17%. By October 2029, bear value is $155.03 and bull value is $413.77.

The weighted forecast is broadly flat: $268.75 in October 2027, $271.04 in October 2028 and $277.87 in October 2029. Against today’s $284.79, those outcomes are losses of 4% and 1%, followed by a 3% gain.

blocks.heading: What has to go right, and what could go wrong for Garmin?

paragraphs.text: Earnings provide the main operating path. The base case starts at $2,189 million in October 2027, anchored by the analyst EPS estimate and a revenue-margin cross-check. It rises to $2,384 million in October 2028 and $2,595 million in October 2029, consistent with the 8.88% long-term EPS-growth forecast.

The bear case uses weaker revenue and normalized margins because Fitness growth may moderate, Outdoor declined in Q2 2026, memory costs are rising and Auto OEM remains loss-making. The bull case reaches $2,354 million, then $2,635 million and $2,951 million as premium demand, aviation, Thailand and Mercedes improve together. Aviation growth in both OEM and aftermarket categories supports that upside, but the acquisitions provide no separately quantified earnings contribution.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Garmin really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is cash from operations minus spending on property and equipment. Garmin’s free cash flow was **$1,362,913 thousand in 2025**, or **18.8% of revenue**. A more conservative measure subtracts stock pay, which compensates employees with shares and can dilute shareholders. That real free cash flow was **$1,196,910 thousand**, or **16.5% of revenue**.

dividend.closing: The full memo also examines Garmin’s business, rivals, management, and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Garmin pay its shareholders?

paragraphs.text: The board authorized up to $500 million of repurchases in February 2026. In June, shareholders approved a $4.20 annual dividend paid in four installments. The dividend is a commitment; the buyback authorization gives management flexibility. Garmin’s cash plan has worked well enough to support both growth and returns, but the public figures still do not show which individual investments created the most value.

The dividend starts from the supplied current rate of $4.20. The base case grows it to $4.60, then $5.00 and $5.40, supported by $1.363 billion of 2025 free cash flow and substantial net cash. The bear case freezes the rate as costs and investment weaken cash conversion. The bull case reaches $5.00, $5.80 and $6.70, requiring sustained earnings strength.

blocks.heading: Does Garmin’s cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is cash from operations minus spending on property and equipment. Garmin’s free cash flow was **$1,362,913 thousand in 2025**, or **18.8% of revenue**. A more conservative measure subtracts stock pay, which compensates employees with shares and can dilute shareholders. That real free cash flow was **$1,196,910 thousand**, or **16.5% of revenue**.

Dividends were Garmin’s largest recurring shareholder payment, while buybacks remained discretionary. In one year shown, shareholder payments exceeded free cash flow, which Garmin could cover from saved cash and liquid investments. That is sustainable only if future operations replenish the reserves.

earnings.title: Garmin earnings and guidance
earnings.meta_description: Garmin reports on October 28, 2026, with guidance for revenue, pro forma EPS, margins, and tax rate; watch Fitness and Outdoor.
earnings.opening: Garmin's next results are expected on October 28, 2026. Garmin investors should watch whether Fitness demand remains strong and new products help Outdoor recover.
earnings.closing: The full memo also covers Garmin's business, rivals, management, and risks.

paragraphs.text: On July 29, management raised its full-year outlook to revenue of US$8,050,000 thousand and pro forma diluted EPS of $10.00. Pro forma EPS is an adjusted earnings measure that removes foreign-currency effects and certain one-off tax items. The supporting assumptions are a 59.7% gross margin, a 27.0% operating margin, and a 16.5% tax rate.

blocks.heading: Did Garmin keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: The targets were $6.300 billion of revenue and $1.675 billion of operating income. Actual results were $7.246 billion and $1.876 billion, respectively. In February 2026, the Compensation Committee certified the result at 175% of target, so the awards vest as 175% of the target share amount in three equal annual installments.

blocks.heading: What are Garmin's last eight quarters of results?

paragraphs.text: Revenue rose **11%** to **$2,022,092 thousand** compared with the same quarter a year earlier. Fitness grew **25%**, while Outdoor declined **2%**. Gross margin rose to **62.4% from 58.8%**, and operating income rose **30%** to **$615,508 thousand**. Higher-margin products helped profit grow faster than sales.

blocks.heading: What should Garmin investors watch next?

paragraphs.text: The immediate checkpoint is the scheduled third-quarter earnings call on October 28, 2026. Investors will look for evidence that Fitness demand remains strong and that new products are helping Outdoor recover. Garmin introduced CIRQA, a screenless fitness band, in July 2026 and launched the fēnix 9 family in August. Strong sell-through would support the raised outlook; discounting or weak demand would suggest that launches are not creating durable growth.

Thailand is expected to begin operating in early 2027 after a heavy capital-spending year. The important signs will be an on-time opening, rising output, healthy utilization, and controlled inventory.
